unit.sep: Model domains/fields,control geometry,observe approved induction and distinguish device/energy/performance evidence.
unit.careers: Illustrative electrical generation,instrument design and science teaching roles.
unit.focus: Magnetisation and demagnetisation; Magnetic fields; Electromagnetic induction; Factors affecting the magnitude of induced electromotive force (e.m.f) (qualitative treatment); Application of electromagnetic induction.
unit.phenomenon: A fictional poster claims a stationary magnet powers every nearby wire and a bell drawing proves actual induction generation.
unit.supportingPhenomena: Domain/field models,four source conductor movements,controlled qualitative factors,daily devices and conditional make-break bell project.
unit.drivingQuestion: How is the study of electromagnetic induction important in our daily life?
unit.content: Magnetisation and demagnetisation; Magnetic fields; Electromagnetic induction; Factors affecting the magnitude of induced electromotive force (e.m.f) (qualitative treatment); Application of electromagnetic induction.
unit.coreCompetencies:
Creativity and imagination: as the learner designs and makes a simple electric bell using locally available materials.
Learning to learn: as the learner carries out experiments of magnetising a magnetic material and demagnetising a magnet.
unit.values:
Unity: as the learner carries out assigned roles when performing experiments to demonstrate electromagnetic induction.
Responsibility: as the learner takes care of the apparatus (U-shaped magnet, galvanometer and straight conductors) while carrying out experiments on electromagnetic induction.
unit.pcis: Life skill; (self-esteem): as the learner explains the methods of magnetisation and demagnetisation.

assessment.instructions: Independent40minutes:5readGEM15,10Section1,10Section2,10Section3,5Section4/check/submit. Use only final reference/prompts;no keys or hints. Qualitative treatment,no numerical e.m.f. derivation. Actual source outcome d experiment/project evidence is assessed separately.

sections.title: 1. Methods and magnetic fields
sections.prompt: Describe two magnetisation methods for soft iron using the domain model,and two conditional demagnetisation methods. Explain low relative retention and why hammering alone does not specify the result. Draw a bar-magnet field pattern with poles,external/internal directions and a compass tangent;state one representation limit.
sections.exemplar: A controlled DC coil or nearby magnet can favour domain alignment;consistent stroking/field-assisted mechanical methods depend on conditions. Diminishing alternating field and suitable heating/disturbance can reduce net alignment under relevant conditions,not as live instructions. Soft iron usually retains less than hard permanent material,not guaranteedzero. Field loops outsideN→S/insideS→N,noncrossing,compass north end tangent;schematic lines are not measured physical threads.

sections.title: 2. Induction conditions and direction
sections.prompt: Using GEM15 geometry,compare stationary,parallel,upward perpendicular and angled motion at comparable speed. Predict a field-only reversal and a field-plus-motion reversal with fixed leads. Explain e.m.f. versus current,why a closed path is needed for the latter,and what actual experiment record is still missing.
sections.exemplar: Stationary/parallel baseline;perpendicular largest among equal-speed cases;angled smaller with nonzero perpendicular component. Field reversal flips reference response;both reversals restore it. Absolute right/left depends wiring. Induced voltage can exist on open conductor,current needs closed conducting path and circuit conditions. Supplied records lack actual learner setup,allfourmotions,roles/observations;outcome d is not certified.

sections.title: 3. Qualitative factors with controls
sections.prompt: Explain how stronger field,faster relevant motion,greater correctly active conductor length and more linked coil turns can affect induced magnitude. State what stays fixed,how orientation matters and why exact multipliers/numerical derivations are not warranted by the given records.
sections.exemplar: Appropriate changes can increase the rate of linked flux change and induced magnitude. Hold other geometry,field/speed,meter/circuit conditions fixed. Parallel motion in stated geometry giveszero;perpendicular movement maximises equal-speed case. Wire length must be properly active and coil turns properly linked;arbitrary loose length is insufficient. Source records are qualitative,not values proving ratios.

sections.title: 4. Applications and actual-evidence scope
sections.prompt: Explain a generator or transformer application with its required change and energy input. Contrast the battery bell’s primary make-break action and soft-iron role. State whether these written answers prove actual induction experiment,bell making,magnetisation/demagnetisation practicals or digital research.
sections.exemplar: Generator converts mechanical input through changing flux;transformer uses changing electrical input/linked field,not steadyDC after transients. Bell battery current magnetises core,armature openscontact,current falls,spring recloses;soft iron releases readily. This is primarily electromagnet action,not free induction generation. Written answers certify none of the actual actions;separate approved observed records are needed.
